title: Service runtime observability: metrics, tracing, dashboards (roadmap)
summary: Working notes and proposal for standardizing runtime metrics (definitions and labels), tracing conventions, and a baseline dashboard set for GPU-backed inference services. Includes alerting thresholds and a phased roadmap for rollout across hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
body:
Context and goals:

This doc collects team thinking for a small, consistent observability surface for our service runtime components (model-serving process, router/proxy, batcher, cache layer). Goal: a minimal set of high-signal metrics and trace conventions that let engineers answer three questions quickly:
 1) Is the system meeting latency & availability SLOs?
 2) Where are tail latencies and errors coming from (model, infra, network)?
 3) Is cost per token within expected band for a workload class?

Why now:
- Dedicated and Private deployments introduce heterogeneity in infra; we need consistent telemetry to compare performance and drive Optimize recommendations.
- New kernel selection logic and continuous batching need new latency breakdowns (tokenization, kv-cache, kernel-exec).

Principles (short):
- Keep the metric set small, high-cardinality by label as needed but avoid exploding series.
- Prefer histograms for latency where we need p95/p99. Use exponential buckets tuned to observed medians.
- Traces are sampled adaptively (higher sample rate on error and high tail requests).
- Dashboards are oriented by persona: SRE incident triage, ML eng performance tuning, Product usage.

Metric definitions (proposed canonical names and labels):
- runtime_request_count{service, model, deployment_tier, route, outcome} -> counter. outcome=success|error|timeout|fallback.
- runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service, model, route, deployment_tier} -> histogram (for p50/p95/p99).
- runtime_inference_token_latency_seconds_bucket{service, model, gpu_type, sequence_bin} -> histogram. sequence_bin ~ short|medium|long (see label rules below).
- runtime_kv_cache_hit_ratio{service, model, route} -> gauge (0..1) computed as hits / (hits + misses).
- runtime_active_batches{service, model, gpu_type} -> gauge (current number of batches).
- runtime_gpu_utilization_percent{instance_id, gpu_type, model} -> gauge (from node exporter/NVIDIA exporter).
- runtime_error_rate{service, model, route, error_class} -> counter (errors / request window used in SLO evaluation).
- runtime_cost_units{service, model, deployment_tier} -> counter (normalized cost units aggregated from infra billing extrapolation).

Label guidance (to avoid cardinality explosion):
- model: only top-level model name (e.g., redwood-7b-v1). No commit hashes. For experimental models use model=experimental.
- route: logical API route (generate, chat, embeddings).
- deployment_tier: hosted | dedicated | private.
- gpu_type: ampere-a10 | h100 | cpu. Keep list finite.
- sequence_bin: short (<128), medium (128-1024), long (>1024).

Tracing conventions:
- Root span: service.request with attributes: request_id, user_tier, model, route, input_token_count, output_token_count, client_region.
- Sub-spans:
  - tokenizer: span name service.tokenizer; attach token counts and tokenization_time_ms.
  - kv-cache-lookup: service.kv_cache.lookup; tag cached=true/false, keys_checked.
  - kernel-execute: service.kernel.exec; attributes: seq_len, batch_size, backend_kernel, runtime_ms.
  - network-e2e: service.network.egress/ingress; attributes: peer_region, rtt_ms.
  - fallback-decision: service.fallback; reason tags (model_unavailable, quota, error).
- Error handling: marks and events should include stack/snippet and error_code.
- Sampling: default 0.1 for requests; for any request with duration > p95 or that results in outcome!=success, increase sampling to 1.0 for the trace. Also sample 100% of requests for canary-deployment model variants for the first 48 hours.

Dashboard sketch (panels and intent):
1) Topline SLOs panel (SRE)
  - p95 and p99 request duration across deployment_tier and model (heatmap).
  - error rate (1m/5m) with alert overlay.
  - percent of requests using fallback path.
  - owners: eng-sre, pager on alert.
  - primary alerts: p99 > 2 * baseline OR error_rate > 0.5% sustained 5m (thresholds adjustable per model class).

2) Tail latency drill (incidents, triage)
  - traces sampled with latency distribution, top contributing spans (kernel-exec, kv-cache).
  - time-correlation with GPU utilization and active_batches.
  - quick links to recent GitHub PRs that touch kernel selection or batching (via linked_artifacts).

3) Cost and efficiency (product/infra)
  - cost_units per 1k tokens by model and deployment_tier.
  - cache-hit ratio and its effect on token cost.
  - batching efficiency: avg tokens per batch and avg batch formation time.

4) Private/Dedicated health (platform)
  - per-customer aggregates for latency and error rates (redact PII).
  - autoscaler activity and capacity headroom.

Alerts (first pass):
- Severity P0 (paging): sustained p99 request duration above SLA for 5m; or error_rate > 1% for 5m. Pager: oncall-sre.
- Severity P1 (channel): sudden drop in KV cache hit ratio > 20% relative to 1h baseline.
- Severity P2 (ticket): average batch formation time > 250ms for 10m.

Instrumentation checklist (developer-facing):
- [ ] Expose the canonical counters/gauges/histograms from the runtime process metrics endpoint (/metrics) using the names above.
- [ ] Ensure exporter includes the standard label set only. Extra labels must be added via RFC and reviewed for cardinality.
- [ ] Add trace spans with agreed names and attributes in the request path (tokenizer, kv-cache, kernel-exec, network).
- [ ] Wire adaptive sampling hook to trace exporter using our sampling library.
- [ ] Add unit tests that assert histogram bucket ranges and label presence for a nominal request.

Rollout plan (phased):
Phase 0 (Q4 2024) - pilot on hosted-api model: redwood-7b-v1 and redwood-13b-v1. Implement metrics and trace spans, dashboards for SRE.
Phase 1 (Q1 2025) - expand to Dedicated; integrate GPU-level exporter and cost_units. Enable cache-hit ratio alerts.
Phase 2 (Q2 2025) - Private deployments: provide an instrumentation guide and a lightweight collector package for air-gapped installs.
Phase 3 (Q3 2025) - Integrate with Optimize recommendations: auto-suggest quantization/batching changes based on cost_units and latency tradeoffs.

Open questions and decisions needed:
- Do we want request-level sample keys to be stored for 7 days for post-incident debug (privacy & storage cost tradeoffs)?
- How aggressive should we be on default trace sampling in hosted vs private? Private customers may prefer lower telemetry by default.
- Finalize cost_unit definition and normalization. Current proposal: normalize to GPU-minutes on h100 equivalent and add per-token overhead for model size. Need finance input.

Immediate next actions (owners):
- Marisol: draft RFC for metric names and label set (due 2024-11-05).
- Jamal: prototype histogram bucket sets for token latency and push to dev cluster (target 2024-11-12).
- Eleni: update dashboards and wire alert channels to oncall-sre (target 2024-12-01).
- Devon: cost_unit model sketch and finance sync (target 2024-11-19).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic: please flag label choices that might create cardinality explosions. If you have a dashboard panel you rely on that requires an extra label, call it out and include a short justification.
- For private deployments we should produce a short 'telemetry checklist' that customers can opt into; add comments in this doc with suggested minimal and extended sets.

Appendix: example queries
- p95 request duration (PromQL-like): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="generate"}[5m])) by (le, model)) by (model)
- cache hit ratio (compute): sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_lookups_total[5m])) by (model)
- cost units per 1k tokens: increase(runtime_cost_units_total[1h]) / (increase(runtime_output_tokens_total[1h]) / 1000) by (model)

Please add comments inline below or in the linked RFC. If you want to prototype alternate bucket boundaries or label sets, add a short note under 'experiments' and tag the owner.

-- Marisol (on behalf of eng-observability)
